limitations: Life expectancy, biological lifespan, and maximum age are different measures.
Long-term survival effects may remain uncertain even after an intervention is developed.
The search is not proof that every relevant clinical program lacks an effect.

our_interpretation: Read the next decade as the ten years ending March 8, 2036.
The plain reading is a doubling of how long humans can typically live relative to the March 2026 baseline, demonstrated by human demographic or clinical evidence.
A change in an aging biomarker, improvement in one disease, or animal lifespan extension does not itself qualify.
The source does not distinguish population life expectancy, attainable biological lifespan, and maximum verified lifespan. These measures must not be interchanged.
Assess the categorical prediction of non-occurrence; a single outcome cannot establish a literal zero probability.
criteria.support_condition: After March 8, 2036, suitable human evidence shows that the specified lifespan measure did not double during the forecast window.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Reliable human evidence establishes a doubling of typical lifespan relative to the same March 2026 baseline by March 8, 2036.
